article.info_title: Policy update: Inconsistent language between the feed and the website
article.info_description: In December, 2024, we are relaxing the supported language policy to allow some differences between your product feed language and website language. Product information including title, description and variant information that are in a different language from your designated feed language will be allowed as long as the majority of the product data matches the feed language. article.info_title: Sharing Data with Researchers on European Parliament Elections
article.info_description: We are glad to announce that we have compiled a dataset of European Parliament (‘EU’) election 2024 related queries in different EU languages to support transparency and engagement with the researcher community. Researchers can apply using this form. Requests will be considered on a case-by-case basis.

Allow us to cache, pretty please.
      As the internet grew over the years, so did how much Google crawls. While Google's crawling
      infrastructure supports heuristic caching mechanisms, in fact always had, the number of requests
      that can be returned from local caches has decreased: 10 years ago about 0.026% of the total
      fetches were cacheable, which is already not that impressive; today that number is 0.017%.

article.info_title: Crawling December: The how and why of Googlebot crawling
article.info_description:
You may have heard that Google Search needs to do a bit of work before a web page can show up in
      Google Search results. One of these steps is called crawling. Crawling for Google Search is done
      by Googlebot, a program running on Google servers that retrieves a URL and handles things like
      network errors, redirects, and other small complications that it might encounter as it works its
      way through the web. But there are a few details that aren't often talked about. Each week this
      month we're going to explore some of those details as they may have a significant effect on how
      your sites are crawled.

article.info_title: #GTMTips: Quickly Duplicate Tags In Google Tag Manager
article.info_description:
There are many reasons why you might want to duplicate your tags (or triggers, or variables, or templates) in Google Tag Manager.
One prime example is server-side tagging, where it’s sensible to first build and validate your tracking setup before migrating fully to a server-side approach.
Alternatively, you might want to collect analytics data to a second property, for example when you want to have a local and a global dataset for site visit data.
